+{"loc":"ELMALILI:54:1-8#3","rows":[{"verses":["54:1"],"words":["وَٱنشَقَّ ٱلْقَمَرُ"],"type":"reports","speaker":"İbn Sînâ","stance":"reports","claim":"Ibn Sina urges withholding judgment on reports of an arif's prayers bringing rain or healing, averting disasters, or affecting animals, since hidden natural causes may underlie such wonders.","anchor":"İbn Sînâ İşârât’ının nihâyetinde “Esrâr-ı Âyât”","mentions":[]},{"verses":["54:1"],"words":["*"],"type":"interpretation","speaker":"İbn Sînâ","stance":"reports","claim":"Ibn Sina traces unseen natural effects to psychic constitution, properties of elemental bodies, or celestial forces, associating magic with the first, miracles and saintly wonders with the second, and talismans with the third.","anchor":"İbn Sînâ İşârât’ının nihâyetinde “Esrâr-ı Âyât”","mentions":[]},{"verses":["54:1"],"words":["*"],"type":"interpretation","speaker":"İbn Sînâ","stance":"reports","claim":"Ibn Sina says denial without proof is as irrational as credulous assent; when a report seems strange, suspend judgment unless there is proof it is impossible, because nature holds many marvels.","anchor":"İbn Sînâ İşârât’ının nihâyetinde “Esrâr-ı Âyât”","mentions":[]},{"verses":["54:1"],"words":["وَٱنشَقَّ ٱلْقَمَرُ"],"type":"interpretation","speaker":"author","stance":"rejects","claim":"Elmalılı says Ibn Sina wrongly treated the heavens and celestial bodies as simple, non-elemental, untouchable substances whose lack of rectilinear-motion inclination made them incapable of being torn or corrupted.","anchor":"İbn Sînâ teessüf olunur ki ilm-i tabîî nâmına nazariyesinde yanlış bir fikre zâhib olmuş","mentions":[]},{"verses":["54:1"],"words":["وَٱنشَقَّ ٱلْقَمَرُ"],"type":"interpretation","speaker":"author","stance":"holds","claim":"Elmalılı argues that allowing a body's inclination to circular motion while excluding inclination to straight motion is an unsupported contradiction, since direction is accidental to motion and any obstacle needs a separate account.","anchor":"Birinin câiz olabildiği bir yerde diğeri de câiz olabilir.","mentions":[]},{"verses":["54:1"],"words":["وَٱنشَقَّ ٱلْقَمَرُ"],"type":"interpretation","speaker":"author","stance":"holds","claim":"Elmalılı says stars and their spheres are composed of elemental matter like Earth and can undergo generation and corruption, in accord with the scientific and philosophical views of his time.","anchor":"Onlar da Arz gibi ecsâm-ı unsuriyeden mürekkeb ve binâen‘aleyh kevn ü fesâdı kābildirler.","mentions":[]},{"verses":["54:1"],"words":["وَٱنشَقَّ ٱلْقَمَرُ"],"type":"interpretation","speaker":"author","stance":"holds","claim":"Given theories that the Moon separated from Earth, a philosopher may read the verse as a past event, but cannot use that reading to deny either the prophetic miracle or a future splitting at the Resurrection.","anchor":"Buna göre de وَٱنشَقَّ ٱلْقَمَرُ","mentions":[]}]}
